How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Chair’ s
discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the Community Services
Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the Commission
before the meeting for their consideration but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted
after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  October 5, 2026

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Ana Casillas, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Fall 2026 Afterschool Program & Summer Camp recap

Fall 2026 Afterschool Program
The San Gabriel Afterschool program is offered at four elementary schools (Coolidge,
McKinley, Washington and Wilson) for 1st-5th graders and now runs from the bell until
6pm. This year we extended the program’s end time from 5pm to 6pm and added in a
biweekly STEAM activity component. The program also started charging a monthly fee for
participants. The program offers a variety of activities including daily homework time, bi-
weekly arts and crafts, outdoor recreation activities, games, and special monthly
highlights. Currently, the program boasts 162 participants in total for the 2026-2027
school year.

Day Camp
The Community Services Department held its Summer Day Camp program from June 8
through August 14. The camp for youth, ages 5- 12 ran from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and
was held at Coolidge Elementary School for Weeks 1-9 and the Mission Playhouse
Glassroom for Week 10.

The camp, which had a total of 951 enrollments, offered a variety of themed weeks
featuring arts & crafts, swim days at Smith Park Pool, structured games, STEAM activities,
reading time, field trips, and spirit days. This year the camp introduced weekly culinary
activities and fun activity stations. Additional popular highlights of the camp were field
trips to the Aquarium of the Pacific and Ninja Adventure Park, Summer Camp Family
Potluck Night, and the talent show on the last day of camp. Next summer, staff plans to
enhance the spirit days and also try to incorporate guest speakers.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  AUGUST 3, 2026
   George Young representing San Gabriel Sea Gulls made a comment on Sea Gulls Highlight.
  The San Gabriel Sea Gulls had seven major swim meets and they went well. The boys placed
  17th overall for Southern California Swimming, and Sean Phan, a resident and smith park pool
  employee, won an event (50 butterfly) and will attend college on a swim scholarship. The pool
  heater was very hard on the team; however, it pulled them all together and those who stayed
  were serious and had intense practices which allowed the pre-summer to really launch them
  in the right direction. George is glad to see the plans for the renovations to the pool and would
  like to show his support for the renovations.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  AUGUST 3, 2026
   Commission suggested that we can give theatre rental discounts to theatre groups
